expectations.text: States the first release of a crate must be published manually with an API token, and the trusted publisher is added afterwards
expectations.evidence: crates.io only lets you add a trusted publisher to an existing crate

expectations.text: Scopes that first-release token to `publish-new`/`publish-update` and a crate-name pattern with the default 90-day expiry, and revokes it after the trusted publisher is added
Enables the crate's 'Trusted Publishing only' setting after migration so tokens can no longer publish it
Rejects empty placeholder crates, stating name-only placeholders are banned on crates.io and names are never reassigned on request
expectations.evidence: Name-only placeholders are banned; team does not reassign

expectations.text: States that crates on crates.io cannot depend on crates from other registries, so the public SDK cannot pull the internal `cindervale-auth`
expectations.evidence: crates.io rejects dependencies on other registries

expectations.text: Prescribes `publish = ["<registry>"]` in each internal crate's `Cargo.toml` so a private crate can never reach crates.io

Writes `.cargo/config.toml` with a `[registries.<name>]` sparse index and `credential-provider`, and `registry = "<name>"` on each internal dependency, stating Cargo never falls back from a named registry to crates.io
expectations.evidence: Cargo never falls back from a named registry to crates.io

expectations.text: Tells users to pass `--locked` to `cargo install`, or Cargo ignores the published `Cargo.lock`
Recommends dist (cargo-dist) for prebuilt binaries with `github-attestations = true` (off by default) and `[package.metadata.binstall]` so `cargo binstall` fetches the archive instead of compiling
Publishes with `cargo publish --no-verify` from the same commit after the auth action, with `cargo publish --dry-run` and `cargo package --list` in the build job
Adds a team owner (`cargo owner --add github:cindervale:<team>`) so access survives people leaving
States `cargo yank --version` (reversible with `--undo`) is the rollback primitive, and whole-crate deletion exists only within 72 hours or under the low-usage rule
Recommends a credential provider (`cargo:macos-keychain`, `cargo:wincred`, `cargo:libsecret`) on laptops because `cargo login` stores tokens in plain text
Rejects `pull_request_target` and `workflow_run` triggers for the publish workflow
expectations.evidence: crates.io rejects the first two for trusted publishing
